title: fix(app-shell): follow the served schema’s one $ref indirection in SchemaForm
body:
Fixes #9912

## What the measurement said, and where it disagrees with the card

`SchemaForm` follows no pointer: on `4e27a9b6c`, `$ref` or `$defs` in that file is **0**, and the control `anyOf` in the **same command** is **21 occurrences over 20 lines** (the card's 17 was taken before PR #9911 restructured the region). That half of the card holds.

The rest of it did not survive re-derivation. Reproducing the served derivation exactly as `/meta/types` produces it — `z.toJSONSchema(getMetadataTypeSchema(type), { unrepresentable: 'any' })`, the degenerate-derivation retry, then `stripUnauthorableProperties` — and walking each document **structurally** (never stringified, and a pointer is never followed while enumerating, so the walk is over the document tree and cannot cycle):

| reading | count |
|:--|--:|
| metadata types enumerated | 27 |
| types whose derivation is non-degenerate | 26 |
| types carrying a definition dictionary | 7 |
| pointer nodes anywhere | 35 |
| **pointer nodes outside the dictionary** | **14** |
| of those, pointing at the recursive Query-DSL `FilterCondition` | 12 |

The card named 17 property rows; the honest figure is 14 nodes, and only 10 of them are in a `properties` position — the other 4 sit in `items` or `additionalProperties`, which is the half the card did not enumerate and the only half this change moves.

## Which rows reach an author today

Measured by rendering the real `SchemaForm` against the real derivation and the real spec form, then reading the DOM — not by reading the source.

| row | author surface today | reachable | rendered face |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `report.runtimeFilter` | `ReportDefaultInspector` then `SchemaForm` | **yes** — `mdf-runtimeFilter` | `textarea` |
| `report.blocks[].runtimeFilter` | same, joined reports | **yes** — `mdf-blocks.0.runtimeFilter` | raw JSON |
| `dashboard.globalFilters[].optionsFrom.filter` | `DashboardDefaultInspector` then `SchemaForm` | **yes** — `mdf-globalFilters.0.optionsFrom.filter` | raw JSON |
| `field.summaryOperations.filter` | `SchemaForm` when the field type is `summary` | **yes** — `mdf-summaryOperations.filter` | raw JSON |
| `app.navigation`, `app.areas[].navigation` | `SchemaForm` — `app` registers no default inspector | **yes** | raw JSON |
| `agent.lifecycle.states` | `SchemaForm` — `agent` registers no default inspector | **yes** — `mdf-lifecycle.states` | `textarea` |
| `dataset.filter`, `dataset.measures[].filter` | `DatasetDefaultInspector`'s own visual `FilterConditionField` | no — never reaches `SchemaForm` | a condition builder already |
| `dashboard.widgets[].filter` | `widgets` is in the inspector's `hiddenFields`; a selected widget goes to the scoped widget inspector | no | — |
| `field.relatedListFilter` | not declared by the spec's `field` form | no — absent across four field-type drafts, with `mdf-expression` present in the same renders as the control | — |
| `object.fields[].relatedListFilter`, `object.fields[].summaryOperations.filter` | `object.fields` is curated by `ObjectDefaultInspector`; a single field is edited through the `field` form | collapses onto the two `field` rows above | — |
| `object.validations[]` | not declared by the spec's `object` form | no | — |

## The shape chosen, and why the other two are wrong

**Chosen: resolve the pointer against the document's own definitions, before the widget decision, with a cycle guard.**

⭐ But the reason is **not** the card's reason, and the difference is the whole finding. Every `*.filter` / `*Filter` row the card named points at **one** definition — the recursive Query-DSL `FilterCondition`, whose derivation is `allOf: [ an open record, { $and / $or / $not } ]`. No top-level `type`, no top-level `properties`, so `resolveFieldFace` answers `raw-json` **both before and after** resolution. Measured, per row:

```
report.runtimeFilter    face TODAY: raw-json   face IF RESOLVED: raw-json
dataset.filter          face TODAY: raw-json   face IF RESOLVED: raw-json
field.relatedListFilter face TODAY: raw-json   face IF RESOLVED: raw-json
```

The rows that move are the pointers in an array-items or record-value position that name an object shape. Rendering the real `app.navigation` property, same component, differing only in whether the definitions the document already carries are reachable:

```
CONTROL (definitions unreachable) => mdf-navigation
   textareas: 1  inputs: 0
SUBJECT (definitions reachable)   => mdf-navigation-label, mdf-navigation.0.id, mdf-navigation.0.label,
   mdf-navigation.0.icon, mdf-navigation.0.order, mdf-navigation.0.badge, mdf-navigation.0.badgeVariant,
   mdf-navigation.0.visible, mdf-navigation.0.requiredPermissions, mdf-navigation.0.requiresObject,
   mdf-navigation.0.requiresService, mdf-navigation.0.type, mdf-navigation.0.objectName,
   mdf-navigation.0.viewName, mdf-navigation.0.recordId, mdf-navigation.0.recordMode,
   mdf-navigation.0.filters, mdf-navigation.0.runAction, mdf-navigation.0.children
   textareas: 3  inputs: 12
```

One opaque JSON control becomes 18 addressable row fields. With the spec's own `type: 'repeater'` field spec the control arm is worse still — a repeater with **no** sub-fields at all, the objectui#3379 shape.

**Rejected: fix the derivation upstream so it emits no bare pointer.** Out of this repo, and — measured — it would not help the rows the card is about either: inlining the `FilterCondition` target reaches the same `allOf` husk and the same JSON editor. Reported, not attempted.

**Rejected: decide the JSON fallback is correct for these rows and pin that instead.** Correct for the `FilterCondition` family — the spec's own `report` form declares `widget: 'json'` on `runtimeFilter`, so the JSON editor is the intended control there, not a fallback — and that is exactly what the negative case below pins. It is wrong for `app.navigation`, where a real editor is derivable from a shape the document already carries.

⛔ One thing deliberately **not** done: routing these rows to the registered `filter-builder` widget. It consumes a rule ARRAY, while a `FilterCondition` is an object keyed by field with `$and` / `$or` / `$not`. Writing one into the other's slot is precisely the class-(c) trap the card is filed under — metadata the runtime refuses.

## How the probe traverses the indirection

The subject is an indirection, so nothing here tests a node before resolving it. Enumeration walks the document as a **tree**: `properties` / `patternProperties` / `$defs` / `definitions` / `dependentSchemas` are read as MAPS whose keys are author-chosen names and whose values are nodes; `items`, `additionalProperties`, `not`, `if` / `then` / `else`, `propertyNames`, `contains` are read as nodes; `anyOf` / `oneOf` / `allOf` / `prefixItems` as arrays of nodes. A pointer is recorded, never followed, during enumeration — so the walk terminates on a self-recursive definition without a guard. Resolution is a separate pass, and it is the one that carries the stack guard.

## Ablation

Subject chosen as the value the two implementations DISAGREE about — `app.navigation`. `report.runtimeFilter` answers identically under both, which is why it is a negative and not an ablation subject.

```
HEAD blob   = 4dc5f8ca43187fd6fb3648ae981c1bb66bf7aef7
pre-mutate  = 4dc5f8ca43187fd6fb3648ae981c1bb66bf7aef7      (tree matches HEAD before the mutation)
anchor occurrences BEFORE: 1   inject occurrences BEFORE: 0
anchor occurrences AFTER : 0   inject occurrences AFTER : 1
post-mutate = c5885d78e3042fbe0e4bf02fa95d3623efa4896f      (hash moved, so the mutation landed)

ABLATED RUN command-exit=1
  x SUBJECT: an array-items pointer becomes a repeater with real per-row controls
  v NEGATIVE: the FilterCondition rows the card named keep the JSON editor
  x the self-recursive arm keeps its indirection instead of hanging the walk
  x a row's own keywords win over the definition it points at
  v a document with no definitions to resolve against renders exactly as before
  Test Files  1 failed (1)       Tests  3 failed | 2 passed (5)

post-restore = 4dc5f8ca43187fd6fb3648ae981c1bb66bf7aef7      (equals the HEAD blob)
git diff HEAD byte count: 0
inject occurrences after restore: 0
```

The mutation script traps on EXIT / INT / TERM with absolute paths, treats an empty hash as a FAILURE, restores with an explicit `HEAD` rather than a bare checkout, and proves the restore by hash equality AND an empty `git diff HEAD`. Both negatives stay green through the ablation, which is what makes them measurements of "unchanged" rather than passengers.

⭐ The negative is pinned in both directions a resolver could go wrong: a row that is NOT a pointer keeps the control it has today in the SAME render, a document with no definitions at all renders identically, an unresolvable pointer keeps the last-resort editor, and the self-recursive arm keeps its indirection instead of hanging the walk.

## Collateral: what a whole-corpus render says

Every type in the spec's form registry, rendered twice through the same component — once with the document's definitions reachable, once with the dictionary removed (which is byte-for-byte the pre-change behaviour) — and the two sets of form-field DOM ids diffed:

```
object 0/0 · field 0/0 · hook 0/0 · report 0/0 · dataset 0/0 · view 0/0
app gained 1 lost 1 (mdf-areas.0.navigation -> mdf-areas.0.navigation-label: the same field, a better face)
dashboard 0/0 · position 0/0 · action 0/0 · page 0/0 · agent 0/0 · tool 0/0
skill 0/0 · flow 0/0 · permission 0/0 · email_template 0/0
```

## Verification

| run | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/ apps/console/ packages/core/` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — 978 files, 11556 passed, 1 skipped |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` (after building the dependency closure; the fresh-worktree TS2307 run is a prerequisite, not a red gate) |
| `eslint .` in `packages/app-shell` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — 1184 files, 0 errors, 3040 warnings (the tree's standing baseline; the added block contributes none) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — 1 source file of 1 released package, 1 changeset declared |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm -s check:control-bytes` | exit 0 — 7995 tracked text files scanned |
| `pnpm -s check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 — 0 new citations |

Test sweep enumerated by the concept, one command carrying a control: 45 test files name the `SchemaForm` family, the control term `useMetadataClient` hits 109 in the same run. They live in `apps/console`, `packages/app-shell` and `packages/core` — and since the package barrel re-exports `SchemaForm` and `apps/console` consumes it through the src alias, a narrowing below the package is not provable, so all three trees were run whole.

Pending-changeset sweep: one command over `.changeset/` matched 13 bodies on the `SchemaForm` / `inferWidget` / `resolveFieldFace` / raw-JSON family (`$ref` and `$defs`: 0 hits, with `SchemaForm` firing 17 times and `objectui` hitting 1426 files in the same run as controls). None is made false by this diff — the two nearest, `9830-nested-anyof-predicate-string-arm.md` (`'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`) and `9859-repeater-grid-widget-detectors.md` (`'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`), describe the detector chain, which this change does not touch and whose pins stay green in the sweep above. No amendment.

## What did not survive reading, for whoever picks this up

- The triage seat's delivery boundary asked for a lit-up control on "any one of the 17 rows". ⛔ That is not available: all 12 `FilterCondition` rows answer identically before and after. The lit-up control here is `app.navigation`, a pointer in the same served corpus that the card's enumeration did not reach.
- `dataset.filter` and `dataset.measures[].filter` already have a real visual condition builder in `DatasetDefaultInspector`. The card reads them as author-facing raw-JSON rows; they are not.
- `field.relatedListFilter` and `object.validations` are declared by the schema and omitted by the spec's form, so no amount of pointer resolution reaches them. That is a producer-side gap, not this renderer's.
